top_choice_rationale: P001 is one identifiable invention, the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock, followed by a decisive demonstration at about 10^-18, reproduced across laboratories and species for years. The two-person Katori and Ye allocation is short and defensible, the citation is scoped to the lattice-clock architecture and not to record numbers, and it has already enabled new tests of gravitational redshift, varying constants and dark-matter couplings. P002 is the broader scientific story and I rank it second, but the author record of the 2018 experiments has not been tested against the supplied names and eight years is a short maturity, so attribution remains open. Either award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: Profile-based conflict: long-running collaboration with Anne L'Huillier and papers with the Lund attosecond group, and joint work with Ursula Keller's ETH group; none of these is a documented tie to Katori or Ye or to the B022 names, but atomic-physics proximity to B012 could be raised, and a collaboration with Luca Argenti and others is also on record.
